name: Seared Pork Chop with Pumpkin Purée & Walnut-Basil Dressed Green Beans

instructions.primary_message: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
680 g green beans
1 ½ lemons
1 small pkg fresh basil

instructions.primary_message: Trim green beans. Transfer to a large baking sheet pan.
Roughly chop walnuts. Add to the baking sheet with the green beans, drizzle with oil, then season with salt and pepper. Toss to combine and spread out in an even layer.
instructions.secondary_message:
⅓ cup walnuts
extra virgin olive oil
salt
black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake, tossing halfway through, until green beans are fork-tender and walnuts are golden, 12-15 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, pat pork chops dry with paper towels and place on a plate. Season with salt and pepper on both sides.
instructions.secondary_message:
6 pork chops, boneless
salt
black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Working in batches if necessary, add chops and pan-fry until golden brown and cooked through, 3-4 minutes per side. Transfer to a clean plate, loosely cover with foil, and set aside. (Reserve skillet with drippings for later use.)
Meanwhile, place pumpkin, cream, maple syrup, vinegar, and spices in a medium bowl. Whisk to combine the pumpkin mixture.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ½ (425 g) cans pure pumpkin purée
177 ml heavy whipping cream
pure maple syrup
1 ½ tbsp red wine vinegar
salt
black pepper
¾ tsp nutmeg, ground

instructions.primary_message: Return skillet (with drippings) to medium heat. Add pumpkin mixture and cook, stirring often, until purée is warmed through, 3-4 minutes. Remove from heat and cover to keep warm.
Meanwhile, zest and juice lemons into a small bowl.
Pick basil leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl with the lemon, along with oil, Dijon, maple syrup, salt, and pepper. Whisk to combine the dressing.
instructions.secondary_message:
extra virgin olive oil
1 ½ tsp Dijon mustard
pure maple syrup
salt
black pepper

instructions.primary_message: When the beans and walnuts are done, drizzle with dressing, then toss to coat.
To serve, divide pumpkin purée and green beans between plates. Top pumpkin with pork and enjoy!
